title: This Turtle Swam 12,774 Miles Across the Pacific in 647 Days

scenes.text: This turtle swam 12,774 miles across the Pacific Ocean.
Scientists put a satellite tag on a leatherback and followed it for 647 days.
It crossed from Indonesia all the way to the coast of Oregon.
Leatherbacks weigh up to a thousand pounds and can dive about 4,000 feet.
They can stay under for 85 minutes, deeper than any other turtle.
A thousand pound turtle. Twelve thousand miles. One ocean.

description:
A tagged leatherback sea turtle swam 12,774 miles from Indonesia to Oregon in 647 days.
Leatherbacks are the largest turtles on Earth, can weigh up to 1,000 pounds, and dive to about 4,000 feet.
Where would you swim first? Comment below.
first_comment: How does a turtle find its way across an entire ocean? Scientists are still working on the full answer. What's your guess?
